evidence.reference_title: Mutation in KANK2, encoding a sequestering protein for steroid receptor coactivators, causes keratoderma and woolly hair.
evidence.snippet: Using whole-exome sequencing, we identified a homozygous missense c.2009C>T mutation in KANK2 in the patients (p.Ala670Val).

nodes.description: The homozygous KANK2 p.Ala670Val missense variant alters SIP, an ankyrin-repeat protein that normally sequesters steroid receptor coactivators (SRCs) in the cytoplasm and so restrains transcriptional activation by steroid receptors, including the vitamin D receptor. The variant is predicted to abolish this sequestering ability; the precise molecular defect has not been demonstrated biochemically.

nodes.description: Systemic retinoid therapy (acitretin 25 mg daily) combined with topical keratolytics, with liver function and lipid monitoring, was followed by marked improvement of the keratoderma within two months in one clinically diagnosed type IV patient. No KANK2-specific or controlled treatment data exist.
